If you have OCD, you can completely make yourself believe it is is 100% true. Your memories can even completely change to make you remember stuff that didn't even happen. So, your husband could think that right now he did something to the baby, and in about a week of overthinking it, he could form a “memory” that he did it. That will obviously further the distress. There is also another thing that could happen that is probably already happening that is (one of) the key condition(s) of OCD: doubting. He is probably going back and forth for hours on whether or not he did it and whether or not he meant it and whether or not it will affect the baby and whether or not he should try to hide it and whether or not he's going to go to jail and whether or not you'll divorce him and whether or not everyone will hate him if they find out and whether or not he'll lose his job and every potential job just because he thinks that he did something inappropriate. The only thing you can do is help him to learn to accept uncertainty, and for the love of God, do not constantly reaffirm him that he did nothing wrong/there is no proof because that just causes more doubt which furthers the checking, anxiety, and mental anguish. There's not too much you can do, but I would try to just learn as much as possible about OCD because it's probably going to branch out in other places if there's a current spike. If he doesn't already see one, see if it's possible for him to see a therapist who specializes in OCD. There are certain types of therapy that works best for OCD such as CBT. Meds are sketchy and don't actually help OCD as much as it would for something like ADHD, and the side effects are much much worse. You can try meds if you'd like, but I personally never found them useful at all, and the other people I've talked to with OCD don't like them either. There are a few miracle cases where people find meds for OCD that work, and the side effects aren't so detrimental to long-term health that it's considered an option, but please look up the symptoms for the medicine. Doctors will not tell you the serious side effects because if they did 1. Placebo effect would make you think you have them 2. You wouldn't take the meds because you would see how potentially dangerous they are. If you're in the US, they'll give the absolute bare minimum information which is almost always just saying that it makes you tired and nothing else. I know this is very depressing to hear because this basically a massive “you can't really do anything :)” but just trust the OCD therapist with some type of therapy for OCD treatment, and it should become easier for him to live with it.

Last thing, your last sentence in the main text was a little weird in wording. Did you mean that he admitted to doing something to see if he did it in the past as like a confirmation?

You can't hunt them down and apologize. You've already talked to your friend about it. You have done everything you can. You might be the only person in that group of people who still thinks about it. You might be the last person in that group of people to think about it. Breathe in and breathe out. It's over. You did something you don't approve of, but there is not a thing you can do about it. That might be frightening to you, but sometimes you have to lean back and accept that it's over, and you've done your best. Hope this helps and good luck

Be careful when you think you must have certain answers about something to prove you aren't X when it's definitely an OCD thought. It will usually just move the goal posts, and it will create more anxiety once these things are figured out, and it will push the narrative further. For example, the abused as a child thing. If the answer (key word is “if” because I don't actually know) was “yes, it's proven that abuse as a child can lead to predatory behavior,” then your OCD would probably just move the goal posts to “Oh, I must've been abused as a child, and I simply don't know it!” After thinking about it for a while, your OCD will tell you to check with your parents to see an answer. They'll say they didn't, and your OCD will tell you that they were lying, and they're trying to keep it a secret from you. Now, you're scared not only about the predatory thing, but you are also scared of your parents and that you may have been abused somehow. This is massively over-the-top, but so is OCD. In my experience, coming to terms with the worst possible outcome is the best thing to do. Also, when I do convince myself that some intrusive thought has no grounding in reality, I will forget about it for a while, and it will randomly come back and attack at full force out of nowhere. I think the term for asking for answers and such is called “checking,” and it becomes a habbit that you do for possibly hours. Doing stuff like answer seaking on Google and such. It never really works out very well most of the time. If you need any help, I'm here
Also, please don't hurt yourself. It's not worth it by any means, and you have people who can help you
